steps.title: Isolate mononuclear cells
steps.instruction: Isolate mononuclear cells (MNCs) from bone‑marrow blood samples (volume 1–25 ml) by Ficoll density‑gradient centrifugation at 800 rpm for 20 min.

steps.title: Select CD34+ cells
steps.instruction: Immediately select BM CD34⁺/lin⁻ cells using the Diamond CD34 Isolation kit and an autoMACS Pro separator (Miltenyi Biotech) following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Deplete lineage‑negative cells
steps.instruction: Deplete magnetically labelled lineage‑positive cells; obtain CD34⁺/lin⁻ cells from the lineage‑negative fraction using CD34 Microbeads (Miltenyi Biotec) as per the kit protocol.

steps.title: Dilute and count cells
steps.instruction: Dilute the cell suspension in Trypan blue and count cells with a hemocytometer.

steps.title: Calculate cell number
steps.instruction: Calculate the number of cells per sample using: Total cells counted × dilution factor ÷ (number of squares) × 10⁴ cells ⁄ ml × 2 ml cell suspension.

steps.title: Preserve high‑count samples
steps.instruction: If the counted CD34⁺/lin⁻ cells are ≥10 000, preserve them in 50 µl RNAlater and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Preserve low‑count samples
steps.instruction: If the counted CD34⁺/lin⁻ cells are <10 000, resuspend the cells in 10 µl Prelude Direct Lysis module (NuGEN, AC Leek, The Netherlands) and store immediately at –80 °C.

steps.title: Perform FISH on small sample
steps.instruction: Perform fluorescence‑in‑situ hybridisation (FISH) on a small aliquot of selected CD34⁺/lin⁻ cells (≥10³ cells) fixed in Carnoy’s solution using standard methods.

steps.title: Acquire FISH images
steps.instruction: Image the FISH slides with a Zeiss Axioskop 2 fluorescence microscope equipped with a 100‑W UV lamp (Osram), a ProgRes MF CCD camera (Jenoptik), and ISIS System Software (MetaSystems).

steps.title: Count interphase nuclei
steps.instruction: Count at least 200 interphase nuclei per suitable specimen (optimum = 300 nuclei).

steps.title: Read all nuclei
steps.instruction: Read each available interphase nucleus, even in sub‑optimal specimens.

steps.title: Report FISH results
steps.instruction: Report results according to the International System for Human Cytogenetic Nomenclature (ISCN).

steps.title: Isolate total RNA
steps.instruction: Isolate total RNA from BM CD34⁺/lin⁻ cells that were stored in RNAlater.

steps.title: Skip RNA extraction for low‑count cells
steps.instruction: Do not extract RNA from cells stored in Prelude Direct Lysis module (NuGEN) because of low cell number; instead start downstream RNA processing directly from these cells.

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA from extracted RNA
steps.instruction: Prepare cDNA from 50 ng of previously extracted RNA using the Ovation Pico WTA System V2 kit (NuGEN) together with the Encore Biotin Module Kit (NuGEN), following the manufacturers’ instructions.

steps.title: Hybridise cDNA (standard input)
steps.instruction: Hybridise the cDNA to Affymetrix Human Transcriptome Array 2.0 (HTA 2.0) on the GeneChip platform (Affymetrix).

steps.title: Scan GeneChip
steps.instruction: Scan the GeneChip using an Affymetrix GeneChip Scanner 3000 according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA from low‑count cells
steps.instruction: Prepare cDNA from 3 µl of BM CD34⁺/lin⁻ cells resuspended in Prelude Direct Lysis module (NuGEN) using the Ovation One Direct System kit followed by the Encore Biotin Module Kit (NuGEN), adhering to the manufacturers’ instructions.

steps.title: Hybridise cDNA (low‑input)
steps.instruction: Hybridise this cDNA to Affymetrix HTA 2.0 on the GeneChip platform (Affymetrix).

steps.title: Preprocess microarray data
steps.instruction: In R 3.4.2, summarise HTA 2.0 probe sets with the RMA function of the ‘oligo’ Bioconductor package (v3.4) and perform principal‑component analysis (PCA) using the ‘prcomp’ function from the ‘stats’ package (v3.4.2).

steps.title: Generate MvA plots
steps.instruction: Create M‑vs‑A (MvA) plots with custom scripts, displaying the relationship between average log intensity (A) and log intensity ratio (M) for each sample pair.

steps.title: Quality‑check and correct batch effects
steps.instruction: Examine PCA and MvA plots before and after preprocessing; if batch effects are observed (due to differing RNA‑extraction or GEP protocols), correct them with the ‘ComBat’ function from the ‘sva’ R package.

steps.title: Normalize intensities
steps.instruction: Normalize the data to remove intensity bias using the ‘normalize.quantiles’ function of the ‘preprocessCore’ R package.

steps.title: Differential expression analysis
steps.instruction: Compare 12‑month versus diagnosis samples with a two‑class SAM test (function ‘samr’ in the ‘samr’ R package); control false‑discovery rate with the Benjamini‑Hochberg procedure, applying a cutoff of 0.05 to define significant genes.

steps.title: Functional clustering of genes
steps.instruction: Submit the significant differentially expressed genes to the DAVID online tool (https://david.ncifcrf.gov/) for functional clustering based on annotation term co‑occurrence.

steps.title: Select protein‑coding genes for analysis
steps.instruction: For analysis, use protein‑coding genes that have a unique EntrezID in the Affymetrix NetAffx annotation (HTA 2.0 Transcript Cluster Annotations, Release 36, 7/6/16).
